'''Chesu 车苏''' is a [[Loloish languages|Loloish]] language spoken in southern [[Shuangbai County]], northern [[Xinping Yi and Dai Autonomous County|Xinping County]], and [[Eshan County]] in [[Yunnan]], [[China]].

The Chesu refer to themselves as ''{{IPA|tsu su³³pa²¹}}''<ref name="Yunnan1955"/> or ''{{IPA|tɕi²¹su⁵⁵pho²¹}}'' (Jishupo 吉输颇).<ref name="Long2007">Long Luogui 龙倮贵. 2007. ''Honghe yizu zuyuan zucheng ji qi renkou fenbu'' [http://www.yixueyanjiu.com/news/3/z_3_4338.html 红河彝族族源族称及其人口分布] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052922/http://www.yixueyanjiu.com/news/3/z_3_4338.html |date=2017-12-22 }}.</ref> Yunnan (1955) reports that Chesu is spoken mostly in Taihe Township 太和乡, with a population of over 360 as of 1955.<ref name="Yunnan1955">[http://www.doc88.com/p-97281176367.html 云南民族识别参考资料] (1955), p.40</ref> ''[[Ethnologue]]'' reports 3,300 Chesu speakers out of an ethnic population of 6,600 people, as of 2007.<ref name=e25/>

Bradley (2007) reports that Chesu is closely related to [[Nasu language|Nasu]] and classifies it as a ''Nasoid'' language. Chesu speakers consider themselves to be a separate ethnic group from the surrounding [[Nisu language|Nisu]] speakers. The Chesu language is currently being replaced by [[Nisu language|Nisu]] and Chinese.<ref name="Bradley2007">Bradley, David. 2007. East and Southeast Asia. In Moseley, Christopher (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, 349-424. London & New York: Routledge.</ref>

Chesu is also used as a second language by [[Shansu language|Hlersu]] speakers.<ref name=e25/>
